name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It preserves fine details in complex scenes—like foliage or machinery—where other upscalers blur edges or lose depth. The trade-off is slower processing time, but the 0.5%+ quality gain justifies it for high-stakes renders.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscalers won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because the core problem is motion blur in source footage, not resolution loss—adding depth won’t sharpen faces, it’ll just slow the pipeline. Instead, test RealVisXL’s face-focused upscaler on a controlled sample: if face fidelity improves by 0.5%+ without new artifacts, it’s the better lever; if not, the real fix is a temporal denoiser before upscaling.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL 5.0’s face-preserving upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline now. Faces in high-stakes renders are the weakest link—this model specializes in keeping eyes, teeth, and skin textures sharp even when source footage is blurry or low-res. The trade-off is higher VRAM usage and slower speed, but the 0.5%+ face fidelity gain directly impacts the most critical visual element. Depth-aware upscalers won’t fix the core problem; RealVisXL attacks it head-on.
[dispatched 4 workers: worker-6666, worker-5097, worker-5448… — done, dissolved]

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s face upscaler won’t fix EXCAVA’s core flaw—it’s a bandage on motion blur, not the source. The real risk is wasting cycles on a tool that can’t address the root problem: unstable source footage. Test a motion-deblur model (e.g., DiffusionBeasts’ *Deblur* or Topaz’s *Video AI*) first—if face fidelity improves *without* upscaling, that’s the 0.5% win.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Test DiffusionBeasts’ Deblur on EXCAVA’s motion-blurred footage first—if face fidelity improves, swap in RealVisXL 5.0’s face upscaler afterward. Result: a face-fidelity gain of at least 0.5% without wasting cycles on depth-upscalers. Owner: Gearbox.
